A.why: The terraced descent is a real shape, but no shot has a subject: flat ice to a far slab skyline, or a block at the lens.

B.best_shot: the crater from the rim, seed 1
B.why: The crater of terraces round a spired isle is the most distinct shape here, but the photo lacks a foreground and the aurora is invisible from the game camera.

C.why: Ridged lake ice and a causeway give real leading lines and depth, but there is no subject at the end of the road and the ridges leave little open ground.

D.why: A decent road-to-gate perspective, but the round bowl with dark patches is close to the moor, and two cameras are blank or blocked.

E.why: An avenue of towering pillars gives the run's only frame with real scale, and the barrow wisps read from the game camera; the nave still needs a subject at its end.

F.why: The best gothic mood, with dead woods round a curling road, but the layout is the moor's oval bowl and winding road repainted.

notes: No candidate has a store-page photo: every set has at least one camera jammed against a slab, and the seeds of each map barely differ. Four of six reuse the same faint under-ice line as their effect, and nobody built a single tall subject (a tower or arch) that the best shot is framed around.
